items.title: Javon Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I’m reading a book about the bassist Pops Foster

ctx.x: schools, like Notre Dame, are starting pretty quickly, as early as they can in August, to try to get it all in before Thanksgiving. So that’s what they’re trying anyway. So again I try to case-by-case students that are thinking about coming to the University of Hartford, Jackie McLean Institute of Jazz, they’re interested to know what’s going on and obviously all I can let them know is what I receive from the university because I don’t really know. But you’re right, there’s a lot of questions from faculty, from…

This is just an aside but I’m reading a book about the bassist Pops Foster and in the book he talks about playing on the steamboat lines on the Mississippi and in 1917 we had to shut down for a couple of months because of the flu. I said wow. That was over a hundred years ago and the same type of thing happened to musicians and everyone at that time.

Right. Like they say at some point things kind of come and you can almost kind of point your finger in the history of time when there’s been an occurrence similar. And so we’re living through it in our lifetimes.
